about: The Rust library that reads dates and times written in words, like "tomorrow" or "2 hours ago", for the uutils date tool.

prs.title: A time zone followed by DST now reads as summer time
prs.broken: GNU date lets you write a zone like EST followed by the word DST to mean that zone's summer time. Here it was rejected as an invalid date.
prs.changed: A DST word after a standard time zone now adds the hour. Zones that are already summer time still reject it, as in GNU.
prs.matters: Dates written this way give the same time as GNU date.

prs.title: Three more time zone names are understood
prs.broken: The date parser rejected the time zone names MET, HAST and HADT, which GNU date accepts.
prs.changed: The three names were added with the same offsets GNU date uses, and checked against every short name GNU knows.
prs.matters: Dates written with these zone names now parse the same as with GNU date.
